source_observation_ecology: Honeybees take pollen from male flowers although native Eufriesea nigrohirta legitimate pollinators collect resin; about 99 percent of male pollen removed by honeybees; legitimate bees leaving robbed flowers carried less than 0.1 percent of pollen compared with unrobbed visits.
source_observation_structure: Dioecious male and female individual plants independently observed in original studies; male pollen resource differs from resin reward sought by legitimate Eufriesea. This cannot be coded automatically as the focal source-pollen architectural division.
source_observation_timing: Original 2002 study records 3-day male pollen presentation with about 66 percent on first day; 2004 study reports honeybee visits including pre-anthesis; no experimental randomization of reproductive organ architecture.
source_reported_effect: Negative association between honeybee visit frequency on males and seed production of females; direct reproductive route evidence but not a same-scale structural alternative fitness comparison.
missing_for_formal_architecture_coding: Matched shared-vs-separate genotype construction cost; male siring fitness; genotype-level heritability and origin of dioecy; independent structure coding.

source_observation_ecology: Social bees collect pollen or pollen plus nectar from bat-pollinated flowers; bats are considered likely legitimate pollinators.
source_observation_structure: Flowers are described as bat-adapted with exposed pollen, but article abstract does not establish function-specific new anther modules or an alternative viable organ.
source_observation_timing: Original four-tree comparison found pollen theft more intense where anthers dehisced earlier than in trees dehiscing later; bee access generally precedes bat foraging.
source_reported_effect: Qualitative observational association of earlier anther dehiscence and higher pollen robbery across four trees; not randomized timing selection and not direct seed/siring fitness.
missing_for_formal_architecture_coding: Same-flower controlled developmental dosing alternatives and viable fitness; heritability of exposure timing; anatomical cost and evolutionary origin.

source_observation_ecology: Long-proboscid Gnoriste fungus gnat transfers pollen while accessing dilute nectar; syrphids and bumblebees remove pollen but typically do not visit female-phase flowers.
source_observation_structure: Flower has strong protandry: male and female function separated across floral phase, two receptive stigmas; this is a source-observed temporal sexual function feature, not a proven source-specific module construction.
source_observation_timing: Original report says robber visitors generally appear on pollen-bearing male phase flowers after earlier legitimate fungus gnat visits; source phase order is ecological and floral phenology, not an experimentally changed program.
source_reported_effect: Original pollen loads and open vs hand pollination support legitimate and inefficient visitor distinction; no experimental alternative structural lifetime fitness contrast.
missing_for_formal_architecture_coding: Genotype-level reversibility; alternate viable spatial and delayed programs; causal floral timing effect on mating fitness; history of floral phase evolution.

source_observation_ecology: Kirk 1987 laboratory assay measures pollen grains eaten by thrips including Actinidia deliciosa; estimated about 0.2 to 0.7 percent of average flower pollen production per thrips per day.
source_observation_structure: The original pollen-feeding assay does not test kiwi floral architectural response or role-specific anther modules.
source_observation_timing: Experimental thrips feeding rate depends on insect life stage and temperature; no tested developmental flower timing or co-active function optima.
source_reported_effect: Per-insect pollen consumption experimentally quantified, not a field reproductive success or anatomy-selection effect.
missing_for_formal_architecture_coding: Plant architecture and phenology in matched original same-taxon field study; legitimate pollen transfer fitness; structural alternatives; genetic origin.

source_observation_ecology: Bombus haemorrhoidalis is the effective pollinator whereas Apis cerana removes pollen without contacting the receptive stigma.
source_observation_structure: Original morphology describes a narrow passage between anther-stigma column and labellum, plus long nectar tube. Bumblebees push the column and contact both anther and stigma; honeybees can collect pollen without stigma contact.
source_observation_timing: Fresh-flower passage geometry and access differ from flower aging; no source assay of an evolved time-staggered new pollen module.
source_reported_effect: Field pollinator-vs-robber performance is source-tested; functional access filter within preexisting flower is observed, not an independently evolved organ origin.
missing_for_formal_architecture_coding: Manipulated width/geometry or genotypic structural alternatives with joint fitness; structural construction cost; evolutionary ancestry and changes.

source_observation_ecology: Large hermit hummingbirds act as pollinators; insects including Trigona take pollen but do not pollinate, and floral parasites puncture flowers.
source_observation_structure: Existing original abstract gives hummingbird pollination vs robber damage; no source-specific anatomical functional division or new module identified from available text.
source_observation_timing: More than 90 percent of Aphelandra flowers received pollen-collecting bees by midmorning in source report; floral puncture before noon was also common.
source_reported_effect: Approximately 40 percent of Aphelandra flowers had style damage according to source abstract; high antagonistic activity is observed but no source-aligned reproductive fitness counterfactual.
missing_for_formal_architecture_coding: Primary study full-text anatomy and structural variants; direct same-flower functional role partition; independent K; genetic transition.
